problems.test: systems page rendering hero has the h1, lead sentence and diagram
problems.evidence:
systems-render.test.ts takes the closest ancestor of the h1 that contains the lead as the hero: `const hero = ancestorWhere(h1, main, (e) => norm(e.textContent).includes(norm(SYSTEMS_LEAD)));`. It then expects the diagram inside it: `expect(texts).toContain('Agent orchestration')`. three-fixes-render.test.ts requires the hero grid to have exactly two children, with the text column holding both h1 and lead and the diagram outside it: `expect(textCol.contains(h1)).toBe(true); expect(norm(textCol.textContent)).toContain(norm(SYSTEMS_LEAD)); ... expect(textCol.contains(d)).toBe(false);`. The task says the same: "text in the left column ... the diagram in the right column", and the plan says "a text column holding the eyebrow (if any), the h1 and the lead

, followed by a diagram column". So the closest ancestor of the h1 containing the lead is the text column (or something inside it). That element never contains the diagram SVG, so this test can't pass alongside the new layout.
problems.fix: Find the hero as the whole hero section instead of the closest element containing the lead. For example, climb from the h1 until the parent is main or contains #agentic (as three-fixes-render's bandOf does), or use h1.closest('section'). Then assert that this section contains the lead and an `svg text` labeled 'Agent orchestration'.
